location: Nauvis - New Dawn - Ash Processing Sector
summary: Today’s efforts shifted back to expansion — this time pushing west. The pressure is coming from production layout constraints. Acetylene requires lime, and while I’ve been producing lime for concrete, the excess has simply been stockpiled. Space is tightening, and the current layout isn’t sustainable for what comes next.

The solution is clear: a dedicated sector. I’ve begun carving out space for a more permanent concrete and steel production area, along with cleaner routing for all required inputs. If done correctly, this should free up enough room to finally establish acetylene production without compromising existing systems.

Most of the expansion work is now complete. The defensive perimeter is in place, and the majority of the ground has been paved. Only a small section remains unfinished — minor, but I’ll close that gap tomorrow before moving into full construction.

One unexpected development — the starter iron patch has finally been fully exhausted. What was once the backbone of early production is now silent. In its place, I’ve gained something just as valuable: space. This opens up new opportunities for logistics and restructuring closer to the core base.
This next phase won’t be quick. Concrete, steel, and acetylene form a more complex chain, and it will require careful planning to avoid introducing new bottlenecks while solving existing ones.

Research continues to support efficiency rather than expansion. After briefly unlocking seaweed processing, I redirected focus toward quality-of-life improvements. Today I completed Basic Crafting Speed 4 and Basic Inventory Size 4. Small gains, but they reduce friction in every task I perform.
